What is Pitch?

Collaborative presentation platform built for teams, with real-time co-editing, a strong template system, analytics on how recipients engage with a shared deck, and AI assistance for generating and refining content.

Best for

Team-built decks with recipient engagement analytics.

Main features

  • Real-time multiplayer editing with cursors and comments
  • AI deck generation and text refinement
  • smart templates and a large gallery
  • brand-locked custom templates and shared asset library
  • video and voiceover recording onto slides
  • link sharing with per-viewer analytics (time per slide, completion)
  • version history and slide-level assignment
  • workspace roles and permissions
  • PowerPoint and PDF export.

Practical use cases

  • Co-building a fundraising deck with a distributed founding team
  • a sales team sending decks and seeing which slides prospects actually read
  • recording a video walkthrough onto a deck for asynchronous review
  • maintaining a brand-locked template library.

Who is it for?

  • Startups, sales teams, agencies and distributed teams who build decks collaboratively.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium per-seat subscription

Plans described in the source

Free/Starter $0 with unlimited presentations, limited AI credits and basic collaboration. Pro around $20-25/user/mo ($16-20 annually) with custom templates, advanced analytics, private folders and priority support. Business around $40-50/user/mo with brand controls and admin management. Enterprise custom with SSO. Annual billing roughly 20% cheaper. Verify - Pitch has restructured tiers and its market position has shifted.

Free plan

Yes - a genuinely generous free tier with unlimited presentations and basic collaboration.

Free trial

Yes - Pro trials offered; the free tier is substantial enough for real evaluation.

Usage limits to consider

Free tier limits AI credits, custom templates, analytics depth and private sharing. Seat-based pricing on paid tiers.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Best real-time collaboration in this group - genuinely Google-Docs-like multiplayer editing on slides
  • recipient analytics showing time spent per slide is extremely useful for sales follow-up
  • the free tier is unusually generous
  • video recording onto slides supports asynchronous work well.

Limitations to consider

  • AI features are less advanced than Gamma's - Pitch is a collaboration tool with AI added, not an AI-first tool
  • the company has gone through restructuring and strategic uncertainty, which is a real adoption risk
  • PowerPoint export loses fidelity on complex slides
  • RTL and Arabic support are limited
  • smaller template ecosystem than incumbents.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android

Languages

  • English interface; content in any language, RTL support limited

API access

Limited; some integrations available

Integrations and exports

  • Google Drive, Figma, Unsplash, Giphy, Slack, Notion, Airtable, PowerPoint/PDF export, HubSpot (analytics)

Evaluation notes

Pitch's purchase case is collaboration and analytics, not AI generation. Assess vendor stability during procurement given the company's recent restructuring before standardising a team on it.
